In summary, our research is concerned with
the time-averaged aerodynamics of sharp and blunt trailing-edge airfoil geometries in both forward and reversed flows.
the time-averaged aerodynamic characteristics of a NACA0012 airfoil, an elliptical airfoils, and a DBLN-526 airfoil at static angles of attacks from 0 to 180 deg at a Reynolds number Re=1.10×105.
the aerodynamics of aerofoils at high incidence angles and in particular with the influence of the trailing edge geometry on the aerodynamic forces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blunt trailing-edge airfoil is the better choice for high-lift performance in both forward and especially reverse flow.
the time-averaged aerodynamics of the NACA 0002 and DBLN-526 are similar, and both are significantly better than the NACA 0012.

the elliptical airfoils have a better time averaged performance compared to the NACA 00-12 in reverse flow, but that the NACA 00012 has a better time averaged reverse flow performance compared to the DBLN 526.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aerodynamics of a blunt airfoil is significantly different than that of a sharp airfoil.
the aerodynamic behavior in reverse flow is very different from the forward flow.
the blunt trailing-edge airfoil has lower drag in reverse flow, while the sharp trailing-edge airfoil exhibits lower drag in forward flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time-averaged aerodynamic performance of a sharp trailing-edge airfoil in reverse flows is significantly worse than that of a blunt trailing edge.
the elliptical airfoils are more efficient in reverse flow, and the DBLN 526 airfoil is more efficient in forward flow.
the drag of the elliptically blunted trailing-edge airfoil is significantly lower than a flat trailing-edge airfoil in reverse flows.
